assertions.content: Defendants 1 and 2 are barred from executing the decree or taking possession of the disputed land for one month following the payment of Rs. 8,000 to Defendant No. 3.
assertions.speaker: The decree imposes a temporary bar on execution and possession pending payment.

assertions.content: Defendants 1 and 2 must execute a new Kabuliyat within one month of payment, accepting modified terms including a reduced commission rate of 2a. 6p. per ton.
assertions.speaker: The decree mandates execution of a new instrument with specific financial conditions.

assertions.content: Defendant No. 3 must execute a new patta embodying a minimum royalty of Rs. 6,000 and a commission rate of 1a. 9p. per ton, replacing the original terms.
assertions.speaker: The decree requires Defendant No. 3 to formalize altered royalty and commission obligations.

assertions.content: If Defendant No. 3 fails to execute the modified patta and Defendants 1 and 2 fail to execute the new Kabuliyat, the original rafanama remains valid with adjusted royalty and commission rates.
assertions.speaker: The decree provides a fallback mechanism where the original instrument prevails if new terms are not executed.

assertions.content: The compromise decree alters the status quo ante by reducing royalty rates, minimum royalties, and the area of coal land in the Singhs' possession.
assertions.speaker: The court analyzes the legal effect of the document's changes on the parties' status.
